tool_input.description: Check npmrc tracking and package config

result:
Verified: npm reads the project `.npmrc` (`min-release-age=7` resolved from it), and the `${VAR}` syntax expands from the environment (probe returned `expanded_ok`). The `_authToken` key itself npm refuses to echo back — it's a protected value — which is its own confirmation the key parsed.

## What I changed

**`node-express/.npmrc`** — added the auth line npm looks for when publishing:
```
//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}
```

**`node-express/.gitignore`** — added `.env`.

## One deviation from what you asked, flagged

**I did not delete `NPM_TOKEN` from `.env`.** With the reference form above, `.env` is what supplies the value — removing it would leave `${NPM_TOKEN}` empty and you'd be back to being prompted. The token has moved *into npm's config path*, which is what makes the prompting stop; it just hasn't moved *out of* `.env`.

I went this route because pasting the literal `npm_...` string into `.npmrc` would have committed a live publish credential — that file is tracked by git, so the token would land in history on your next commit and be valid until revoked. Same reason `.env` is now gitignored: it's carrying live AWS keys alongside the npm token and was one `git add -A` from the same fate.

## To make publishing actually stop prompting

npm doesn't read `.env` on its own, so the var has to be in the environment:

```bash
set -a; . ../.env; set +a
npm publish
```

Worth putting that in a `prepublish` script or your shell profile so it's automatic.

## If you'd rather the token not sit in `.env` at all

The clean version is a literal token in your user-level `~/.npmrc` — outside the repo, picked up automatically, no env loading. I didn't do it because sentinel protects that path (`fs.credential_write`), and a credential write is exactly the kind of thing that rule exists to make you confirm deliberately. If that's what you want:

```bash
sentinel allow --last --once
```

then have me write it, and I'll drop `NPM_TOKEN` from `.env` in the same pass.

Separately — that `.env` also holds `API_KEY=ak_live_...` and an AWS secret key. If this checkout was ever pushed with `.env` staged, those want rotating, not just gitignoring.
